title: What We Know For Certain — Definitive Conclusions from 1421 Knowledge Entries
methodology: Automated text mining + keyword extraction from knowledge base

category_a_proven_beyond_doubt.description: Harvey t>3.0 OR confirmed 10+ times across diverse tests

conclusions.title: VIX Sufficiency for VT Strategy
conclusions.summary: VIX alone captures sufficient information for the VT strategy. No additional factor (VRP, momentum, term structure, VVIX, credit spreads, yield curve, INDPRO, Yang-Zhang, AAII sentiment, VXEEM, SKEW, put/call ratio, macro) adds statistically significant improvement.
key_statistics: VRP: positive 86% of time, not directional signal
STLFSI4, credit spread, yield curve: theta ≈ 0
conclusions.implication: Stop searching for VIX supplements. Use VIX alone for VT.

conclusions.title: 12/VIX as Irreducible VT Kernel
conclusions.summary: weight = min(12/VIX, 1.0) is the simplest effective VT rule. All complex overlays (SMA, MACD, dual momentum, HAR ensemble, regime-switching) fail to beat it with statistical significance.
key_statistics: 3-row lookup table retains 97.4% of continuous Sharpe
conclusions.implication: 12/VIX is the reference strategy. Any new method must beat it.

conclusions.title: Prediction ≠ Application (QLIKE ≠ Sharpe)
conclusions.summary: Better volatility prediction (lower QLIKE) does NOT translate to better VT strategy performance (higher Sharpe). This is the central paradox of the research program.
key_statistics: HAR-ABS: DM t=-15.45 (best predictor) but LOWEST VT Sharpe
NLP sentiment: Granger-causes RV (p<0.001) but VT Sharpe +0.001
Taiwan SSVS: OOS R²=15.6%, DM t=5.70 but untradable (c2c gap)
conclusions.implication: VT strategy is not sensitivity to prediction accuracy. Focus on risk management, not prediction.

conclusions.title: Daily QLIKE Ceiling
conclusions.summary: GARCH(1,1) extracts all information from daily returns for 1-step volatility prediction. The ceiling is at approximately QLIKE ≈ -8.95 to -9.05 for SPY.
key_statistics: 4+ independent verifications: GARCH-X, GARCH-MIDAS, HAR, FIGARCH, CGARCH
Ljung-Box on standardized residuals: p>0.30 (5/5 assets clean)
QLIKE ceilings: SPY -8.667, GLD -8.430, EEM -8.248, TLT -8.144
Only 5-min Realized GARCH: -18% pilot improvement (41 days)
conclusions.implication: Stop trying to beat GARCH with daily data. Use 5-min RV if available.

conclusions.title: Leverage Effect Universality & Gamma-Direction
conclusions.summary: The direction and magnitude of the leverage effect (gamma) predicts model selection, VT behavior, and diversification amplification. This is the core proposition of Paper 1.
key_statistics: Spearman rho(gamma, trend_beta) = 1.000 for 7 core assets
GJR wins only when gamma > 0.15 (DM p<0.05)
Standard leverage → trend follower, inverted → contrarian
DM test: 100% prediction accuracy across 9 asset-period pairs
conclusions.implication: Check gamma sign before choosing model. Gold/commodities need symmetric GARCH.

conclusions.title: GJR-GARCH ≥ All Complex Models (Daily SPY)
conclusions.summary: GJR-GARCH(1,1) dominates or matches all tested complex models for daily SPY volatility prediction. It is the complexity ceiling for daily data.
key_statistics: Beats: GARCH, EGARCH, CGARCH, FIGARCH, GJR-HAR, GARCH-X
GJR advantage proportional to return skewness (SPY -0.80 → 0.5%)
Feature contribution: GJR asymmetry -0.55% QLIKE (only significant feature)
conclusions.implication: Use GJR-GARCH(1,1) for equities. Use GARCH(1,1) for gold/commodities.

conclusions.title: VT Universal Crisis Protection
conclusions.summary: VT protects in every crisis tested across multiple asset classes. Protection magnitude scales with crisis severity.
key_statistics: EU Debt +9.4pp, Lib Day +5.7pp, Flash Crash +4.7pp
Even Coffee (JO, extreme inverted leverage) protected
conclusions.implication: VT is universal insurance. Works regardless of gamma direction.

category_b_strong_evidence.description: Confirmed 5-9 times with consistent results across tests

conclusions.title: 50/50 SPY/GLD + 12/VIX Robustness
conclusions.summary: Equal-weight SPY/GLD with 12/VIX targeting consistently ranks as top VT strategy. Gold provides uncorrelated crisis hedge (return correlation ~0.12).
key_statistics: Beats 4-asset Risk Parity, dynamic multi-asset, momentum

conclusions.title: Monthly Rebalancing Optimal for VT
conclusions.summary: Monthly rebalancing beats daily and weekly for VT strategy due to reduced whipsaw and lower transaction costs. Mathematically, rebalancing frequency doesn't affect weights (K23 proof).
key_statistics: K23 math proof: sqrt(h) cancels in Sharpe ratio
Gap alert overlay: only +0.6pp MDD improvement (not worth complexity)

conclusions.title: Target Vol Level Irrelevance
conclusions.summary: All fixed volatility targets (8/12/16/20%) produce identical Sharpe ratios. Target only controls risk level (leverage), not risk-adjusted return.

conclusions.title: EGARCH Numerical Instability
conclusions.summary: EGARCH with Student-t distribution is numerically unstable in rolling forecast applications. It produces extreme variance forecasts that corrupt QLIKE evaluation.
key_statistics: Variance clamping partially helps but doesn't fully resolve

conclusions.title: VIX Day-of-Week Effect
conclusions.summary: VIX exhibits a robust Monday increase (+1.91%, t=5.38) and Friday decrease (-0.87%, t=-3.04), stable across sub-periods. However, exploiting this pattern doesn't improve VT strategy performance.

conclusions.title: Taiwan VT Effectiveness
conclusions.summary: 0050.TW benefits from VT using EWMA own-volatility. US VIX works as proxy via 1-day lag. Taiwan market shows higher amplification (4.6x vs US 2.7x).
key_statistics: EWMA own-vol sufficient (no need for VIX)
VXEEM doesn't beat US VIX (Steiger Z=16.2)

category_c_emerging_evidence.description: Confirmed 2-4 times, promising but needs more replication

conclusions.title: Fixed GARCH Parameters > Rolling Refit
conclusions.summary: Fixed-parameter GARCH outperforms rolling-window refit in VT strategy context. Rolling estimation noise exceeds parameter staleness for short horizons.

conclusions.title: Fear DCA Step Function
conclusions.summary: VIX-based step multiplier improves DCA returns by ~4%. Higher VIX → buy more aggressively. Step function beats linear and continuous alternatives.
key_statistics: +4.0% terminal wealth vs naive DCA (bootstrap p<0.01)
conclusions.needs: Cross-asset, different DCA intervals, longer period validation

conclusions.title: VT = Alpha + Insurance Decomposition
conclusions.summary: VT benefit decomposes into equity reduction cost (-4.50%/yr) and crisis protection (+8.7pp MDD). Net effect depends on regime: costly in low-VIX, profitable in high-VIX.
conclusions.needs: Formal utility framework, more crisis periods

conclusions.title: Piecewise VIX→Vol Superior to GARCH
conclusions.summary: Non-parametric piecewise VIX→vol mapping outperforms GARCH in QLIKE by 13.7%. VIX-vol relationship is not log-linear (power law fails +356%).
key_statistics: QLIKE improvement: -13.7% vs GJR (DM t=-2.07, p=0.039)
conclusions.needs: Longer live track record, cross-asset validation

conclusions.title: Gamma-Trend Following Mechanism (Simpson's Paradox)
conclusions.summary: Hood-Raughtigan claim that VT=trend following is partially an ecological fallacy. Within-regime, trend is insignificant in 3/4 VIX bins. VT is vol-contingent allocation, not trend following.
key_statistics: Overall trend t=20.6 but within-regime t insignificant in 3/4
High VIX regime: anti-trend β=-0.04, t=-4.6
conclusions.needs: More assets, formal ecological fallacy test, journal peer review

category_d_single_findings.description: Important discoveries that are unreplicated or from single experiments

conclusions.title: GARCH Volatility Half-Life
conclusions.summary: SPY GARCH vol half-life is 12-25 days depending on persistence. Current: ~13 days (persistence 0.947). Prediction useful only for ~2 weeks.

conclusions.title: BTC Inverse Leverage & Vol Linkage
conclusions.summary: BTC has inverted leverage (gamma=-0.038, up moves more volatile). Post-2020 BTC-SPY vol correlation jumped from 0.03 to 0.40. BTC vol Granger-causes SPY vol.

conclusions.title: 3-Row Lookup Table Simplification
conclusions.summary: 12/VIX continuous can be simplified to 3-row discrete table retaining 97.4% of Sharpe. Counterintuitively, coarser discretization works better.

conclusions.title: Diversification Amplification (US/EM specific)
conclusions.summary: ETF leverage effect > constituent stock average in US and EM, but NOT in Japan or Germany. Likely due to correlation asymmetry differences.

conclusions.title: Multi-Step GARCH Forecast Convergence
conclusions.summary: GARCH conditional information decays exponentially. Beyond 22 steps (~1 month), forecast ≈ unconditional variance. This explains why daily/monthly VT gives identical weights.

open_questions.description: What we don't know — active research frontier

questions.question: Can 5-min Realized GARCH break the daily QLIKE ceiling?
questions.status: Pilot shows -18% improvement (41 days). Need 500+ days for HAR-RV.
questions.priority: HIGH — only known method to break ceiling

questions.question: Does VT work in true hyperinflation / extreme regimes?
questions.status: Never tested. All experiments in developed/moderate-EM markets.
questions.priority: MEDIUM — theoretical interest, practical for EM investors

questions.question: Is the US VIX → Taiwan lag robust across market regimes?
questions.status: Works in tested period but regime stability unknown.

questions.question: Can ML/DL meaningfully improve VT strategy returns?
questions.status: Current: LSTM/GRU add 0% QLIKE. SOTA hybrids untested.
questions.barrier: Prediction≠Application gap may make this moot
questions.priority: LOW — likely blocked by A3 (prediction ≠ application)

questions.question: Is VIX conditional leverage viable long-term?
questions.status: Live but short track record. TX costs impact unclear.

questions.question: Can overnight gaps serve as supplementary VaR signals?
questions.status: |gap|>1.5% → 9.93% violation rate. But EWMA leads by 1-4 days.

questions.question: Do cross-market vol spillover networks predict crises?
questions.status: Early exploration. Unclear if they add value beyond VIX.

meta_insights.description: Higher-order lessons from the research program

insights.title: Simplicity Wins
insights.content: Across 300+ experiments, the simplest methods consistently match or beat complex alternatives. 12/VIX beats every overlay. GARCH(1,1) matches every variant. 3-row table beats continuous. This is not coincidence — it reflects the fundamental information content limit of daily returns.

insights.title: Null Results Are the Majority
insights.content: ~39% of experiments produce null results. This is expected and healthy. Each null result narrows the search space and reinforces A1 (VIX sufficiency) and A4 (QLIKE ceiling). Failed attempts are evidence, not failures.

insights.title: The Prediction-Application Gap Is Fundamental
insights.content: A3 is perhaps the most important finding. It explains why decades of vol forecasting literature hasn't produced better investment strategies. The gap exists because VT performance depends on WHEN you're right (crisis timing), not HOW right you are (QLIKE).

insights.title: Gamma Direction Is the Missing Variable
insights.content: Before this research, model selection was asset-agnostic. A5 shows that gamma sign determines whether GJR, GARCH, or symmetric models are optimal. This is a genuine contribution to the literature (Paper 1).

insights.title: Cross-Asset ≠ Cross-Market
insights.content: Findings that hold across US assets (SPY, QQQ, TLT) don't always transfer to other markets (Japan, Germany). Amplification is US/EM specific. VIX lag to Taiwan works but needs monitoring. Always test cross-market, not just cross-asset.

insights.title: Harvey (2016) Threshold Catches Most False Positives
insights.content: The t>3.0 threshold from Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016) correctly identifies most spurious findings in our data. 0/9 Harvey tests passed for HAR-VIX ensemble improvements. Cross-OOS caught 53% false positive rate. Both validation methods agree.
